q: Which kind of test is the fastest to run?
why: A unit test checks one small piece with no network, database or browser, so it runs in milliseconds. End to end tests start a real browser and are the slowest.

q: A test with no assertion (no expect) can still pass and still add to the coverage number.
why: Yes. Coverage only counts which lines ran. A test that runs the code and checks nothing passes and looks good in the report. Ask: if I break this line, does a test fail?

q: A test sends POST /api/items to an Express app with a test database and checks the status and the saved row. What kind is it?
why: Several real pieces work together (route, validation, data layer) and the test goes through the front door. A real browser is not involved, so it is not end to end.

q: Which of these are good reasons to keep end to end tests few?
options: When one fails it is hard to see which piece broke
why: End to end tests are slow, can fail for unrelated reasons, and give less exact error locations. But they do find bugs the smaller tests miss, so keep a handful for the flows that matter most.

q: Put the three steps of a good unit test in order.
why: Arrange, act, assert, often called AAA. Keep each test to one reason to fail.

q: What do we call a test that guards an old bug so that it never comes back? (one word)
why: A regression test is any test written to make sure a fixed bug stays fixed. Add one every time you fix a bug.
